title: Incoherent by Design? On the Moral Self-Consistency of LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.15354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used in morally sensitive contexts, yet it is unclear whether they apply ethical principles consistently across situations. A model that can state a moral principle may still violate it when the same scenario is rephrased or reframed. This inconsistency is a problem for any system whose outputs are used to inform moral decisions. If generative systems exhibit internal inconsistency, then the epistemic integrity of AI-mediated systems becomes uncertain. To study this concern, we investigate the stability of moral reasoning in LLMs within a controlled prompting framework across three major philosophical schools of thought: deontology, utilitarianism, and virtue ethics. We construct sets of morally equivalent scenarios in which the underlying situation is held constant while the framing varies to reflect different ethical stances and stylistic perturbations. We then evaluate responses from multiple models, including GP

translated_title: 设计中的不一致？论大语言模型的道德自洽性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于道德敏感的情境中，但目前尚不清楚它们是否能在不同情境下一致地应用伦理原则。一个能够陈述道德原则的模型，在相同场景被重新表述或重新框定时，可能仍会违反该原则。这种不一致性对于任何输出用于指导道德决策的系统来说都是一个严重问题。如果生成系统表现出内部不一致性，那么人工智能中介系统的认知完整性将变得不确定。为研究这一问题，我们在一个受控的提示框架内，考察了LLMs在三大主要哲学思想流派——义务论、功利主义和美德伦理学——中的道德推理稳定性。我们构建了道德上等价的情境集合，其中潜在情境保持不变，而框架变化以反映不同的伦理立场和风格扰动。随后，我们评估了包括GP在内的多个模型的响应。
tldr: 本文通过受控提示框架，系统性地测试了大语言模型在义务论、功利主义和美德伦理学三大哲学流派下的道德推理一致性，揭示了模型在等价情境下因表述或框架变化而产生的道德自洽性缺陷。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically tests the moral reasoning consistency of LLMs across deontology, utilitarianism, and virtue ethics under a controlled prompting framework, revealing self-consistency deficiencies in equivalent scenarios due to phrasing or framing variations.
